title: Casper and the Contact
premise: Financial-crimes investigator Rosalind Pemberton has spent years laundering her own past — a fake identity, a packed go-bag, a lie about where she came from — until a burner phone rings with the voice of Casper, her presumed-dead brother, claiming he's alive inside a laundering network that three governments are secretly protecting. As Rosalind follows the money from London to Frankfurt, she discovers the 'clean money' she audits is the same pipeline that faked Casper's death, and an assassin named Vey is erasing everyone who can prove it. To survive, Rosalind must burn her own fabricated identity, choose between the duty that made her and the found family that saved her, and get the ledger into the hands of a Frankfurt regulator before markets open. In the end she exposes the network at the cost of her old life, keeps Casper, and learns that the truth, like money, is only worth what someone will finally pay for it.
about_author: Sable Kavanagh is a former compliance analyst who traded spreadsheet forensics for fiction after a decade tracing money she was never allowed to name. She writes thrillers from a coastal town she refuses to geotag, where the fog does half her redacting for her.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Rosalind Pemberton's POV. A routine audit of immaculately clean accounts leaves her cold; she checks her go-bag, rehearses her cover story, and notes a colleague's nervous disappearance. Emotional beat: controlled paranoia — a woman who trusts nothing, especially her own tidy life.

chapters.title: Burner, Ringing
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. An unregistered phone appears in her desk drawer and rings: Casper's voice, dead seven years, saying only 'the money remembers.' She traces the call to a London relay and realizes someone wants her found. Emotional beat: grief cracked open by hope, immediately weaponized.

chapters.title: Clean Money, Dirty Hands
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, with a brief Casper interlude. She follows the audit thread to a shell company whose beneficial owner is a ghost — her own cover identity. Casper, meanwhile, moves through the network that holds him. Emotional beat: the horror of seeing your lie reflected back as evidence.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She visits her old handler, Marisol, who warns her off and reveals a government task force has flagged the same accounts — and is burying them. First tail spotted outside Rosalind's flat. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: Vey
chapters.summary: Assassin Vey's POV. A cold, precise chapter: Vey erases a forensic accountant in Rotterdam and is handed Rosalind's file with a deadline. Emotional beat: dread established through calm — we see exactly how professionally Rosalind will be hunted.

chapters.title: Dead Man Dialing
chapters.summary: Alternating Rosalind/Casper. Rosalind engineers a second call; Casper explains he faked his death to infiltrate the network and that its ledger names three governments. He asks her to extract him via Frankfurt. Emotional beat: sibling intimacy rebuilt in fragments, trust on a timer.

chapters.title: Found Family, Found Out
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Her chosen family — pub quiz regulars, her neighbor Dev, her ex-partner Theo — notice she's unraveling. Dev, a hacker, offers help; she refuses and lies again, and it costs her. Emotional beat: the ache of protecting people by shutting them out.

chapters.title: The Task Force That Isn't
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She infiltrates a task-force briefing and learns the 'investigation' is a containment operation; a senior official, Halloway, is the network's government shield. She copies a fragment of the ledger. Emotional beat: duty inverted — the institution becomes the enemy.

chapters.title: Rotterdam, After
chapters.summary: Vey's POV, then Rosalind's. Vey finds Rosalind's fingerprints near his kill and begins to admire her; Rosalind realizes the dead accountant was her informant. Emotional beat: hunter and hunted recognizing each other's competence — respect as a threat.

chapters.title: Ledger of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Rosalind and Dev's POV. Dev cracks the fragment: the network launders through central-bank-adjacent channels, and Casper's death certificate was signed off by Halloway's office. Emotional beat: vertigo — the conspiracy is not above the system; it is the system.

chapters.title: The Extraction Offer
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper negotiates his own extraction, but the network demands the ledger back — and offers Rosalind's life as the price. He pretends to accept. Emotional beat: love against duty from the other side; Casper choosing her over the mission.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She and Casper reunite briefly in a safehouse; old wounds surface — she let the world believe he was dead to protect her cover. They reconcile the math of survival versus truth. Emotional beat: forgiveness that doesn't erase the cost.

chapters.title: Halloway's Dinner Party
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, undercover. She attends a regulator's gala where Halloway quietly threatens her with her own fabricated past: expose us, and your identity dies with you. Emotional beat: power's corruption made polite — menace served with wine.

chapters.title: Burn Notice, Self-Issued
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She decides to destroy her own cover identity before Halloway can use it, torching fifteen years of careful lies. Dev and Theo pull her found family into the plan. Emotional beat: liberation through self-immolation — freedom costs everything you pretended to be.

chapters.title: Vey's Doubt
chapters.summary: Vey's POV. Ordered to kill Rosalind before Frankfurt, Vey reviews the ledger fragment and realizes his previous targets were innocent — he's been the network's janitor, not its sword. Emotional beat: an assassin's conscience igniting.

chapters.title: The Night Train
chapters.summary: Rosalind, Casper, Dev. They move the full ledger toward Frankfurt by rail; Vey boards the same train. A tense, near-silent cat-and-mouse through carriages ends with Vey standing over them — and not pulling the trigger. Emotional beat: terror breaking into improbable alliance.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Morning
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Halloway mobilizes diplomatic pressure to seal the borders and bury the story; a Frankfurt regulator, Aldana, becomes the last honest door. The team races to reach her before markets open. Emotional beat: the machinery of power grinding against a handful of people with a file.

chapters.title: Before the Bell
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Trapped in the Bundesplatz district with the ledger, Vey as reluctant shield, and Casper wounded, Rosalind must choose: leak everything publicly and lose control of the narrative, or trust one regulator. Emotional beat: the loneliest decision of her life, made at dawn.

chapters.title: Frankfurt, Opening
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She hands Aldana the ledger minutes before the open; markets wobble, Halloway's containment fails publicly, and the network's accounts freeze in real time on the exchange floor screens. Emotional beat: catharsis — truth landing with the force of a market event.

chapters.title: The Price of the Truth
chapters.summary: Vey's and Casper's POVs. Halloway, cornered, orders one last erasure; Vey refuses and gives testimony instead, trading his freedom for the record. Casper's survival is officially acknowledged — his death certificate becomes evidence. Emotional beat: redemption purchased at real cost.

chapters.title: After the Audit
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Hearings begin; Rosalind, now officially no one, testifies under her true name for the first time. Her found family surrounds her; Theo stays, Dev grins, Marisol resigns on principle. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning — identity rebuilt from truth instead of lies.

chapters.title: What the Money Remembers
chapters.summary: Rosalind and Casper's POV, closing. Months later, on the coast, the burner phone rings one last time — a wrong number, or a warning that the network had cousins. They let it ring out, go-bag unpacked at last. Emotional beat: earned peace, vigilance retained, love that outlasted duty.
